messages:
jess: Heads-up — got a billing alert for tonight, GPU spend spiked ~6x starting 23:12 UTC. Graph: https://billing.company/alerts/28123 :eyes:

bryan: Oof. Do we have autoscaler events around then?

jess: Yeah logs show a bunch of scale-outs from 23:11 to 23:18. I dumped recent node list:
```
NAME                        MACHINE_TYPE   LABELS
model-train-x7-aaaa         n1-standard-8  gpu_type=T4,gpu_pool=high-mem
model-train-x8-bbbb         a2-highgpu-1g  gpu_type=A100,gpu_pool=highmem
model-train-x9-cccc         a2-highgpu-1g  gpu_type=A100,gpu_pool=highmem
```

jess: note the mix of n1-standard with T4s and a2-highgpu A100s — we never run A100s in this pool normally.

lina: I pushed a tiny TF tweak earlier today to rename the nodepool label from `gpu_pool=high-mem` -> `gpu_pool=highmem` to match new naming. Did not touch instance types.

bryan: Sounds like two different provisioners saw different labels and both created pools. One provisioner maps `gpu_pool==high-mem` -> T4 family (reserved), the other maps `gpu_pool==highmem` -> A100 (uncommitted fallback). Autoscaler ended up provisioning both.

sam: Confirmed in cluster-autoscaler events: it saw two nodegroups for the same nodeSelector and blasted both. Snip from events: `ScaleUp: triggered, nodegroup model-train-A100 targetSize increased by 120` at 23:12.

jess: And because the A100 pool isn't in our reservation scope for that region, cloud fell back to on-demand A100s — expensive. Costbot reported 2,300 USD/hr for the burst. :grimacing:

costbot: Billing alert: "GPU hourly spend exceeded daily baseline by 5200%" — triggered 2026-02-03T23:20:04Z

bryan: Root cause hypothesis: label rename + slightly different instanceSelector logic in an old provisioner -> duplicate pools, plus an autoscaler config in one deploy accidentally set the maxNodeCount too high (2000 vs intended 200) because of a missing divisor in a pipeline variable. A perfect storm.

lina: I own the label rename, will revert the TF change and gate it. I didn't touch autoscaler limits. But I did notice a workflow that builds the desired capacity value as `num_jobs * instances_per_job` and one env var was in minutes not jobs. I'll audit.

jess: Immediate mitigation: I cordoned the A100 nodes and set nodegroup desired=0 to stop new launches. Commands I ran:
```
kubectl cordon model-train-x8-bbbb
gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-size model-train-A100 --size=0 --zone=us-east1-b
```

sam: Also patched autoscaler config to cap max nodes:
```
kubectl patch configmap cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --patch '{"data":{"max_total_nodes":"250"}}'
```

bryan: Good. Long-term fixes: 1) Add label-change validation in infra PRs, 2) reconcile provisioner instanceSelector logic so label synonyms map to the same pool, 3) add a reservation-check preflight that rejects deploying instance types not covered by commitments in a region, 4) add a hard upper limit in autoscaler pipeline to prevent runaway due to env var bugs.

lina: I'll open infra PRs for 1 & 2. Sam can you take 3 (billing/reservation preflight) with cloud cost team?

sam: Yup, putting a ticket in now — COSTOPS-492. Will scope API call to list reservations for region+sku and fail CI if mismatch.

jess: Cost impact estimate for tonight: ~38k USD in extra spend. Finance is pinged. I attached the raw billing slices and the node provisioning timeline to the ticket.

bryan: Quick follow-ups: who rolled the autoscaler change that set the max incorrectly? We should trace the pipeline.

lina: That appears from `infra-deploy` run at 22:58 — a YAML templating bug replaced `/100` with `/1` when env var absent. I'm adding guarded parsing and unit tests.

jess: Notes for postmortem: timeline, root cause (label rename + template bug), mitigations applied, and recommended guardrails. Will draft a short postmortem tomorrow.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-021 (assigned to eng-infra).

bryan: Thanks all. Good catch, quick response. :thumbsup:

jess: tagging @oncall about potential fallout on retries for training jobs — we should throttle enqueuing until pools are reconciled.

sam: throttling queued jobs now.

jess: OK closing the thread for now, will update when postmortem is ready.
